title: Settings
description: The settings of the app: kept in settings.toml of the user's configuration folder, not in the collections folder. It has the connection to Trapper and the like, so what is kept of them is a secret.

AgoutiSettings.description: What an upload to Agouti needs (its public API: https://docs.agouti.eu/api/endpoints.html) — kept here; nothing is uploaded to Agouti yet.

enabled.description: Whether Agouti is used as a place to upload deployments to. (AGOUTI.enabled)

api_key.description: The API key Agouti's support gives, sent as X-API-KEY. (AGOUTI.api_key)

project_id.description: The id of the Agouti project the deployments are uploaded to. (AGOUTI.project_id)

Camera.description:
One of the camera traps — its label (what it is called), optionally its id (the serial number) and its model, as Camtrap DP names
them, and the day it was put into production.

label.description: What the camera is called — the name it goes by in the field.

camera_id.description: The camera's id — its serial number. (cameraID)

camera_model.description: Manufacturer and model, written as manufacturer-model. (cameraModel)

connectivity.description: The mobile network the camera sends its photos through: none when it does not.

power_source.description: What it runs on: cells (AA, AAA… the ones that are changed) or a battery.

battery_removable.description: Whether the battery can be taken out of the camera: only said of a battery, as cells are always taken out to be changed.

in_service.description: The day it was put into production.

research_project.description: The acronym of the research project it belongs to: every one belongs to one (a card or camera without it, as older settings had, waits to be assigned).

status.description: Planned: only in Settings, not in the app. Ready: available, not in the field yet. Active: in use. Archived: out of use for good (see archive_reason).

archive_reason.description: Why it was archived; other when it is none of the others (the status note says it).

status_date.description: The day it stopped being active.

id.description: Its internal id — a UUID the app generates when it is kept, that never changes and is never typed: what the records that refer to it point to.

created_at.description: When it was kept here (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

updated_at.description: When it was last changed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

deleted_at.description: When it was removed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z), if it was: it is no longer listed, but it is kept — nothing is deleted.

dir.description: The data folder, where the app keeps what it makes: its collections (collections/<research project id>/<collection>/<deployment id>), reports and packages go in folders inside it, unless each has one of its own. (DATA.dir)

collections_dir.description: A folder of its own for the collections, instead of the "collections" folder inside DATA.dir: <folder>/<research project id>/<collection>/<deployment id>. (DATA.collections_dir)

reports_dir.description: A folder of its own for the reports of the validations, postvalidations and preprocessings, instead of the "reports" folder inside DATA.dir. (DATA.reports_dir)

storage.description: Where the app keeps its records — the research projects and their locations, visits, cameras and SD cards: "json" (files in the collections folder, the one there is for now). (DATA.storage)

packages_dir.description: A folder of its own for the packages made to upload to Trapper, instead of the "packages" folder inside DATA.dir: <folder>/<research project id>/<collection>. (DATA.packages_dir)

enabled.description: Whether Epicollect5 is used as a source: of visits (its entries are downloaded as a CSV), and of the details of a deployment when it is imported. (EPICOLLECT5.enabled)

unmapped_to_comments.description: What an entry says in an input that is not mapped to any field goes to the comments of the deployment. (EPICOLLECT5.unmapped_to_comments)

project_slug.description: Slug of the Epicollect5 project — the name in its URL (five.epicollect.net/project/<slug>). (EPICOLLECT5.project_slug)

client_id.description: Client id of the Epicollect5 API client app, for private projects. (EPICOLLECT5.client_id)

client_secret.description: Client secret of the Epicollect5 API client app. (EPICOLLECT5.client_secret)

mapping.description: Which input of the Epicollect5 form (its ref) gives each field of a deployment: deployment field -> input ref. (EPICOLLECT5.mapping)

enabled.description: Whether the CSV downloaded from the new WildINTEL Epicollect project can be read for visits. (EPICOLLECTCSV.enabled)

FieldlogSettings.description:
Field records: how the visits of a field trip are read from the file of the field app (an Epicollect download) and what is made of them
(see services.visits_csv and services.visit_deployments).

time_source.description: When a visit happened: created_at, the time its entry was created (UTC); or hour, the date and the hour typed in the form (the wall clock of its location). (FIELDLOG.time_source)

keep_seconds.description: Keep the seconds of the visits in the deployments' start and end written in the logs; off, they are cut to the minute. (FIELDLOG.keep_seconds)

trappers.description: The people who go to the field — suggested when a visit is registered, as who went. (FIELDWORK.trappers)

sd_cards.description: The SD cards of the field work. (FIELDWORK.sd_cards)

cameras.description: The camera traps of the field work. (FIELDWORK.cameras)

roles.description: What each trapper is in each research project: a trapper can have several in the same project, one entry for each. (FIELDWORK.roles)

log_level.description: How much the app logs, to the console and its log file. (GENERAL.log_level)

workers.description: How many images are validated or preprocessed at once — up to the CPUs of the machine pays off. (GENERAL.workers)

default_research_project.description: The acronym of the research project that comes filled in wherever one is asked for; it can still be changed there. (GENERAL.default_research_project)

PostvalidationSettings.description:
Which of the postvalidation checks the wizard shows — and so runs — and
the parameters those that take one start from. They need what the wizard
knows of the deployment: its id, collection, location and dates.

collection_prefix.description: Deployment id starts with its collection. (POSTVALIDATION.collection_prefix)

location.description: The id's location is the one chosen. (POSTVALIDATION.location)

image_count.description: The number of images is like the previous revisions'. (POSTVALIDATION.image_count)

sequence_count.description: The number of sequences is like the previous revisions'. (POSTVALIDATION.sequence_count)

sequence_length.description: The length of the sequences is like the previous revisions'. (POSTVALIDATION.sequence_length)

sd_card.description: The SD card is the one the visit left in the camera. (POSTVALIDATION.sd_card)

photo_count.description: The folder has the number of photos the visit counted on the card. (POSTVALIDATION.photo_count)

sequence_gap_seconds.description: What a sequence is: a new one starts when the gap to the previous image is at least this many seconds. (POSTVALIDATION.sequence_gap_seconds)

min_revisions.description: How many previous revisions of the location the statistical checks need to have to judge — with fewer they are skipped. (POSTVALIDATION.min_revisions)

similarity_method.description: What this revision is compared to: the median or mean of the previous ones, the last one, or the range they span. (POSTVALIDATION.similarity_method)

image_count_tolerance.description: What is similar for the number of images, in percent. (POSTVALIDATION.image_count_tolerance)

sequence_count_tolerance.description: What is similar for the number of sequences, in percent. (POSTVALIDATION.sequence_count_tolerance)

sequence_length_tolerance.description: What is similar for the length of the sequences, in percent. (POSTVALIDATION.sequence_length_tolerance)

tolerance_hours.description: Hours of leeway around the deployment's start and end when checking the image dates — the default of the tolerance the wizard asks for. (POSTVALIDATION.tolerance_hours)

PreprocessingSettings.description:
What is done to the images as they are imported into their collection —
which preprocessing steps a new run starts with, and the values they use.
The wizard lists them before the import, and a run can still switch each off.

resize.description: Resize the images to a width, keeping their proportions. (PREPROCESSING.resize)

resize_width.description: The width, in pixels, images wider than it are resized to. Smaller ones are left as they are. (PREPROCESSING.resize_width)

metadata.description: Add authorship, rights and license metadata (XMP, with ExifTool). (PREPROCESSING.metadata)

owner.description: Who owns the images — the rights holder. (PREPROCESSING.owner)

coverage.description: Where the images were taken, in the coverage text (e.g. Doñana National Park). Blank: the deployment's location. (PREPROCESSING.coverage)

license_url.description: The license the images are shared under. (PREPROCESSING.license_url)

ignore_dst.description: Read the camera's clock as if it never changed to summer time, using the timezone's standard offset. (PREPROCESSING.ignore_dst)

convert_to_utc.description: Give the capture dates (in names and metadata) in UTC. (PREPROCESSING.convert_to_utc)

SdCard.description:
One of the SD cards of the field work — its label, as it is written on it, and optionally its brand, its capacity and the
day it was put into production.

label.description: What the card is called — its number or the label on it (e.g. A12).

brand.description: Who makes it, free text (e.g. SanDisk).

capacity.description: How much it holds, free text (e.g. 64 GB).

in_service.description: The day it was put into production.

research_project.description: The acronym of the research project it belongs to: every one belongs to one (a card or camera without it, as older settings had, waits to be assigned).

status.description: Planned: only in Settings, not in the app. Ready: available, not in the field yet. Active: in use. Archived: out of use for good (see archive_reason).

archive_reason.description: Why it was archived; other when it is none of the others (the status note says it).

status_date.description: The day it stopped being active.

id.description: Its internal id — a UUID the app generates when it is kept, that never changes and is never typed: what the records that refer to it point to.

created_at.description: When it was kept here (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

updated_at.description: When it was last changed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

deleted_at.description: When it was removed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z), if it was: it is no longer listed, but it is kept — nothing is deleted.

Trapper.description:
One of the people who go to the field — {username, name, affiliation, email}. The people are global: they belong to no research project (what each is in a project is
its role, which is the project's). Its `username` is what it is called in the app, as the label of an SD card is, and no two have the same.

username.description: What the trapper is called in the app — required, and unique among the trappers (whatever its case), as the label of an SD card is.

name.description: The trapper's full name, written as it should be on a visit.

affiliation.description: Where the trapper works, free text.

status.description: Whether the trapper still goes to the field: an inactive one is no longer suggested, and an archived one is out of use for good (it never goes back).

trapper_pk.description: Its id in Trapper, when it was taken from there — such a trapper can only be seen here.

id.description: Its internal id — a UUID the app generates when it is kept, that never changes and is never typed: what the records that refer to it point to.

created_at.description: When it was kept here (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

updated_at.description: When it was last changed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

deleted_at.description: When it was removed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z), if it was: it is no longer listed, but it is kept — nothing is deleted.

TrapperRole.description: What a trapper is in a research project — one of the roles of a contributor in Camtrap DP (contributors.role).

research_project.description: The acronym of the research project.

trapper.description: The name of the trapper, as it is in the list of trappers.

role.description: Its role in the research project.

id.description: Its internal id — a UUID the app generates when it is kept, that never changes and is never typed: what the records that refer to it point to.

created_at.description: When it was kept here (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

updated_at.description: When it was last changed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z): written by the app, never typed.

deleted_at.description: When it was removed (ISO 8601, UTC, with a Z), if it was: it is no longer listed, but it is kept — nothing is deleted.

enabled.description: Whether Trapper is used as a place to upload deployments to. (TRAPPER.enabled)

user_name.description: Trapper username (its email — the import form only accepts that). (TRAPPER.user_name)

max_zip_mb.description: The images of each deployment are uploaded in packages of at most this many megabytes. (TRAPPER.max_zip_mb)

ValidationSettings.description:
Which of the "Validate folder contents" checks the wizard shows — and
so runs. Each looks at the folder alone, without knowing the deployment.

camera.description: Same camera (model and id) on every image. (VALIDATION.camera)

exif.description: Required EXIF fields (capture date, camera model and id). (VALIDATION.exif)
